experiments.question: Which rung of the A..F ladder projects each family best?
experiments.hypothesis: Structured opportunity x efficiency models (C/D) and learned models (E/F) beat shrunk averages (A/B).
experiments.method: Walk-forward: A-D are point-in-time formulas whose few hyperparameters (shrinkage k, EWMA halflife, elasticities) were tuned on 2016-2021; E is LightGBM refitted every season on all earlier seasons; F is a non-negative stack fitted on 2016-2021 predictions. Each model gets its own distribution fitted on its development residuals; validation (2022-23) selects.
experiments.data: nflverse 2012-2025 regular seasons; team_pass_attempts n_val=1086, team_rush_attempts n_val=1086, team_points n_val=1086, targets n_val=6373, receptions n_val=6373, receiving_yards n_val=6373, carries n_val=1964, rushing_yards n_val=1964, passing_attempts n_val=1082, completions n_val=1082, passing_yards n_val=1082, passing_tds n_val=1082, anytime_td n_val=7118
experiments.result: team_pass_attempts: best F (val CRPS 4.2570 vs A 4.3159); team_rush_attempts: best F (val CRPS 4.1370 vs A 4.2102); team_points: best F (val CRPS 5.0486 vs A 5.2659); targets: best F_av (val CRPS 1.3844 vs A 1.4531); receptions: best F_av (val CRPS 1.0822 vs A 1.1203); receiving_yards: best F_av (val CRPS 14.3945 vs A 14.7391); carries: best F_av (val CRPS 2.8547 vs A 3.1774); rushing_yards: best F_av (val CRPS 16.6101 vs A 17.6256); passing_attempts: best F_qs (val CRPS 4.7959 vs A 4.8671); completions: best F_qs (val CRPS 3.3753 vs A 3.4516); passing_yards: best F_qs (val CRPS 41.4598 vs A 42.2430); passing_tds: best D_qs (val CRPS 0.5594 vs A 0.5659); anytime_td: best F_av (val CRPS 0.1611 vs A 0.1665)
experiments.interpretation: See per-family tables. Gains over A are game-clustered paired differences on identical player-games.

experiments.question: Does a schedule-adjusted opponent factor (rolling ridge, refitted before every week) plus closing spread/total improve player projections beyond opportunity x efficiency?
experiments.hypothesis: D beats C on validation CRPS.
experiments.method: D = C with team volume from the opponent/environment team model and an efficiency elasticity beta on the opponent's ridge factor, beta fitted by Poisson (Bernoulli for TD) likelihood on 2016-2021 only.
experiments.data: validation 2022-2023, paired on identical player-games, games as clusters
experiments.interpretation: Negative = D better. Opponent effects in the NFL box score are small relative to player-game noise; the gain, where it exists, is modest.

experiments.question: Do the closing spread and total add to the opponent-adjusted team volume projection?
experiments.hypothesis: D (opponent + environment) beats D_opp (opponent only) for team pass/rush attempts and points.
experiments.method: Poisson log-linear elasticities on B (EWMA) fitted on 2016-2021; spread/7 and (total-44)/7 terms; for points log(implied/B).
experiments.interpretation: The closing line carries most of the pregame information on team points and rush volume; pass volume is nearly spread-neutral in aggregate (2016-21: 34.0 attempts as a 7+ point underdog vs 34.6 as a 7+ favourite) while rush attempts rise from 24.4 to 28.5.

experiments.question: Do teammates listed OUT/DOUBTFUL on the final injury report explain part of the opportunity error (the mean_defect 'listing/role' residual)?
experiments.hypothesis: Renormalising a player's share for vacated teammate opportunity, share x (1-vacated)^(-gamma), improves targets/carries projections.
experiments.method: vacated = sum of the listed teammates' EWMA target-per-attempt (carry share) among players who appeared in the team's last 3 games; gamma fitted on 2016-2021 (gamma=1 is proportional redistribution). An 'oracle' version uses who actually did not play (post-game) as an upper bound.
experiments.data: 29.0% of player-games have >5% of team targets vacated by listed teammates
experiments.interpretation: Injury-report availability is the pregame-legitimate part of the role signal; the oracle bound shows how much better gameday availability information could be worth.

experiments.question: How do the frozen winners compare with the incumbent shadow-0.4.0 and the shadow-0.5.0 challenger, replayed walk-forward with their own code?
experiments.hypothesis: The foundation models are at least as accurate as the incumbents.
experiments.method: nfl/incumbent.py replays fit_bundle (seasons 2016..T-1) for T=2017..2026 with the frozen design (0.4.0) and the challenger design (0.5.0, in-memory function swap, no file edits) and scores the incumbents' own pmfs on the same player-games.
experiments.data: validation 2022-2023 and holdout 2024-2025, paired rows present in both
experiments.interpretation: Replay note: the research frame includes current-season games, so defect D1 (live history missing this season) does not affect this replay; the comparison is of model design only, which understates the incumbent's live 2026 error.

experiments.question: How much does the participation convention matter, and how well does pregame information predict participation?
experiments.hypothesis: Final injury designations predict DNP well; most DNPs of role players are flagged.
experiments.method: Candidates = role players (>=2 targets or >=4 carries per game) who appeared in one of the team's last 3 games; P(play | designation) fitted on 2016-21; targets CRPS on the full candidate set (DNP = 0) for 'assume he plays' vs the participation hurdle.
experiments.result: DNP rate 15.8%; Brier designation model 0.0967 vs constant 0.1330; 59% of DNPs carried no designation; among published (not OUT) projections DNP rate 12.2%, CRPS assume-plays 1.457 vs hurdle 1.415
experiments.interpretation: Projections are published conditional on participation (prop void convention); the hurdle is the right object for any consumer that does not void DNPs.

failed_experiments.name: LightGBM (E) as a stand-alone projection
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: E beats the structured D rung only in targets, receptions, receiving_yards, carries; it does not in team_pass_attempts, team_rush_attempts, team_points, rushing_yards, passing_attempts, completions, passing_yards, passing_tds, anytime_td (team families and QB families: too few rows per season for trees). On its own it also extrapolates badly outside its training population (non-RB carries projected 3.4 vs 0.76 realised).
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Use trees only inside a stack and only for players inside their training population.

failed_experiments.name: Vacated targets from teammates listed OUT
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: gamma fitted on development is positive but validation CRPS does not improve (targets D_vac - D +0.0011 [-0.0014, +0.0034]); the oracle version using who actually sat is no better (+0.0009 [-0.0004, +0.0024]).
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Do not spend effort on better absence data for targets; the remaining target error is role (depth chart / routes), not absences. Carries are different (absences matter).

failed_experiments.name: Opportunity x efficiency decomposition (C) on its own
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: For targets C - B -0.0004 [-0.0053, +0.0049]: decomposing into team volume x share does not beat a player EWMA (consistent with research/opportunity, which found the same on 2019-2025); its value is structural (it is where game environment and opponent enter).
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Keep C/D for interpretability and as stack inputs, not as the headline model.

failed_experiments.name: QB efficiency from the generic ladder (pre-fix)
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: Ladder rungs B-D were worse than the season average for QB volume because relief appearances contaminated histories; a seemingly 'robust' EWMA was the problem, not the baseline.
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Condition every role-based history on the role (starts for QBs) before smoothing.

failed_experiments.name: Discretised normal for yards / NB on yards
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: The normal misses the right skew and loses to empirical ratios in every yards family; 0-based NB cannot represent negative yards and is mis-scored by pf_core's out-of-support clipping.
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Empirical (quantile-mapped) residual ratios by mean bin are the default for yards.
